short: Raw-face CNN to LSP (M05, M06) is standard: 82.6% vs 40.0% over Le Cornu and Milner mixes in forced-choice listening (M12); as a whole system it later scores 44.92% vs 14.08% GRID WER (Lip2Wav).
position: The paper [@ephrat2017vid2speech] changes the visual input (M05: full-face frames stacked over K = 9 instead of mouth features) and the estimator (M06: a CNN from raw pixels to LSP, keeping the comparator's 8th-order LPC and unvoiced excitation). Both are standard. The gain over Le Cornu and Milner [@lecornu2015reconstructing], 82.6% against 40.0% audio-only word intelligibility on GRID S4 (Table 2), holds in direction but is confounded by the evaluation (M12): Vid2speech listeners picked each word from the GRID vocabulary (Sec. 4.3); the comparator's listeners typed them. As a whole system under Lip2Wav's protocol (Google ASR, mean of 4 GRID speakers), it scores 44.92% WER against 14.08% for Lip2Wav [@prajwal2020learning] [later]. The OOV-digit test (51.6% against 10.0% chance, Table 3) is a ten-way choice, not open-vocabulary reconstruction.
